page: Vultr voc-m-32c-256gb-1600s-amd is an instance from the Optimized Cloud Compute family, provisioned as a memory-optimized architecture. It features an AMD EPYC processor running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, providing 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU cache layout includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. Memory is substantial, delivering 256.0 GB of RAM, which equates to an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. Local storage consists of a bundled 1600 GB NVMe SSD, and one complimentary public IPv4 address is included. There are no GPUs present on this configuration.

Benchmark results highlight solid multi-threaded computational capabilities and strong execution across specific algorithmic tasks. Stress-ng single-core performance places the instance in the top 10% tier (3113.46), while stress-ng multi-core performance reaches the top 25% (99821.78). In Geekbench testing, multi-core throughput scored 16174.0, complemented by strong marks in software compilation with Clang (41962.0), ray tracing (52832.0), and text processing (2449.0). Geekbench single-core scored in the middle tier at 1851.0. Cryptographic acceleration is supported via hardware AES and SHA-NI flags, helping drive a PassMark CPU encryption score of 33206.25 and a physics score of 7742.86 (top 25%).

Memory throughput and operational tests show balanced, mid-tier throughput. Large-block memory bandwidth registers at 138.44 GB/sec for uncached reads and 65.88 GB/sec for writes. PassMark database operations achieved 11065.57, and Redis SET throughput recorded 47.64 million operations per second, matching expected mid-range cloud performance. In CPU-based machine learning inference, prompt processing reached 57.68 tokens per second on a 7B parameter model, with generation at 20.46 tokens per second. A notable bottleneck appears in single-threaded gzip compression, which landed in the bottom 25% at 23.36 GB/sec, reflecting moderate single-core instruction efficiency for older serial compression routines.

Instruction set support includes AVX, BMI2, and FMA, but lacks AVX-512 and AMX extensions. Given the 1:8 core-to-memory ratio, large local NVMe storage, and solid multi-core metrics, this instance is suited for in-memory databases, large-scale software build systems, analytics caches, and memory-intensive enterprise application serving.
description: Vultr voc-m-32c-256gb-1600s-amd is a memory-optimized server within the Optimized Cloud Compute family, driven by a dedicated AMD EPYC x86_64 processor clocked at 2.0 GHz. It offers 32 dedicated vCPUs (16 physical cores with 2 threads per core), 256.0 GB of system memory (8.0 GB per core), and a bundled 1600 GB local NVMe SSD. While lacking hardware GPUs and AVX-512 extensions, it supports standard AVX, AES, and SHA-NI. Benchmark evaluations reveal top-tier single-core stress-ng performance and strong multi-core throughput across Geekbench, software compilation with Clang, and ray tracing. Memory bandwidth, Redis caching operations, and database operations hold steady within mid-tier categories. Single-threaded gzip compression registers on the weaker end. The platform delivers balanced cost-to-density efficiency for high-capacity memory tasks, making it suited for large relational databases, in-memory caches, software compilation clusters, and mid-scale analytics pipelines.
